title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: JANINE'S WINGS
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Janine Pruitt, forty-six, from Dayton, Ohio.
For twenty years, she has loaded cargo planes at night.
She has never once flown one. Until her dad made a wish.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE WISH
segments.quote: No bird soars in a calm.
segments.author: Wilbur Wright
lines: Her dad Walt fixed jet engines in the Air Force for thirty years.
At eighty-one, he said, I'd love to see the old farm from the sky, just once.
Then she passed the Wright brothers' old bike shop, with a line from Wilbur Wright in the window:
No bird soars in a calm.
That night she signed up for flying lessons.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE BOUNCE
segments.quote: There is no such thing as a problem without a gift for you in its hands.
segments.author: Richard Bach
lines: Her teacher was Mister Abernathy, a retired airline captain in a Hawaiian shirt.
Her first landing bounced three times. Like a basketball.
He smiled and read from his favorite book, by the pilot Richard Bach:
There is no such thing as a problem without a gift for you in its hands.
The gift? She'd been staring at her feet. Now she looked far down the runway.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE CLOUDS
segments.quote: There are old pilots and there are bold pilots, but there are no old, bold pilots.
segments.author: Old pilots' saying
lines: Her first solo day came. So did low, gray clouds.
Janine wanted to go anyway.
Mister Abernathy tapped an old sign in the hangar:
There are old pilots and there are bold pilots, but there are no old, bold pilots.
She waited. Next Saturday, blue sky, she flew alone and yelled the whole way.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE CHECKLIST
segments.quote: One father is more than a hundred schoolmasters.
segments.author: George Herbert
lines: But she kept rushing her checklist. One day she forgot the fuel cap.
Dad brought his old Air Force clipboard and walked the plane with her, touching every bolt.
She thought of an old proverb collected by George Herbert:
One father is more than a hundred schoolmasters.
She never missed a bolt again.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE TEST
segments.author: Marcus Aurelius
lines: Then the big test, with an examiner who never smiled.
Janine's mind raced. What if I fail?
Her hands shook, until she remembered the Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius:
Confine yourself to the present.
So she flew one minute at a time. She passed. The examiner almost smiled.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE FARM
segments.quote: Mystery creates wonder and wonder is the basis of man's desire to understand.
segments.author: Neil Armstrong
lines: One clear morning, Janine flew her dad over the old farm.
The red barn. The creek. The tree he fell out of as a boy.
Walt said, thirty years on jet engines, and I still don't get why we stay up.
Janine quoted Neil Armstrong, another Ohio boy:
Mystery creates wonder and wonder is the basis of man's desire to understand.
Walt pressed his face to the window like a puppy.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Fly into the wind. Find the gift. Wait for blue sky. Learn from Dad. Stay present. Keep wondering.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Fly into the wind. Find the gift. Wait for blue sky. Learn from your dad. Stay in the minute. Keep wondering.
Me? I flew once. I held the armrest so tight, they charged me for it.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
